app.title: METABRIC Survival Dashboard (Streamlit demonstrator)
app.summary: The person opens an overview page that shows cohort headline numbers, the held-out model score and a breakdown of one biomarker. On the survival page they pick a stratification variable and get Kaplan–Meier curves per subgroup with confidence bands, a log-rank p-value when there are two groups, and a written interpretation. On the prediction page they set a single patient profile (clinical values, biomarkers and treatments) with sliders, radios and checkboxes. They get back a recalibrated probability of the event before a fixed horizon, shown on a gauge against the cohort base rate, with a warning about model performance and the model's top global feature importances.

task.text: Compare time-to-event curves between subgroups of a cohort, and estimate the fixed-horizon event probability for one profile entered by hand from a trained, recalibrated classifier.

data.text: A cohort table with one row per patient: clinical measurements, categorical biomarker status, treatment flags, follow-up time and an event or censoring indicator. It comes with a pre-trained classifier bundle that holds training-set defaults, metrics and feature importances.
data.item: a patient with follow-up time, event status and clinical covariates

stage.text: presenting survival comparisons and a trained risk model after the analysis is done, for teaching

mechanism.text: A sidebar radio switches between three pages. The survival page recomputes Kaplan–Meier curves, confidence bands and a log-rank test each time a different stratification variable is selected. On the prediction page, every change to the profile form re-runs the model pipeline and Platt calibrator, then redraws the probability card, the gauge with a base-rate marker, and a fixed feature-importance bar chart beside it.

field.text: Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and fixed-horizon clinical risk prediction in medicine

workflow.name: compare time-to-event curves by group and estimate one profile's risk

steps.here: Processed survival and modelling CSVs plus the raw file are loaded from disk, along with a saved model bundle. Pages that need the data stop with setup instructions if it is missing, and the prediction page still works without it.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Home shows KPI cards (patients, event rate, median survival, held-out ROC-AUC), a donut of ER status, the research questions and the analysis pipeline

A stratification selectbox (ER, HER2, PR, grade, chemotherapy, hormone therapy) redraws one Kaplan–Meier curve per subgroup, each with a 95% band and a group n. A log-rank p-value goes in the title for two-group splits, and a caveat about the selected variable is shown below.

Sliders for age, tumour size, positive nodes and mutation count; a grade selectbox; radios for ER, PR and HER2; checkboxes for three treatments. Every other feature is filled from training-set defaults.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The pipeline's predicted probability of death before 5 years is passed through a Platt calibrator and shown as a percentage card and a gauge, flagged above or below the cohort base rate
A horizontal bar chart of the top five global feature importances from the saved model

distinctive: Censoring is respected: the curves use follow-up time with an event indicator, and the classifier's target is defined at a fixed 5-year horizon
Predicted probabilities are Platt-recalibrated before display, and the cohort's base mortality rate is drawn as a marker on the gauge, not used as a decision threshold
A log-rank test is computed only when the stratification has exactly two groups
Each subgroup gets a fixed caveat, written in advance, warning against causal readings of treatment associations
The held-out ROC-AUC and its bootstrap confidence interval are shown next to every prediction as an educational-use warning

parts.title: Page navigation sidebar
parts.summary: Switches between the overview, survival analysis and prediction pages, and opens on prediction when the local data is missing.

parts.title: Cohort overview
parts.summary: Shows headline cohort numbers and the model's held-out score as KPI cards, a donut of one biomarker's distribution, and the research questions and pipeline.

parts.title: Survival analysis page
parts.summary: Lets the person choose a stratification variable and reads back the subgroup comparison with a written interpretation.

parts.title: Kaplan–Meier curves with log-rank test
parts.summary: Fits a Kaplan–Meier estimator per subgroup and draws survival curves with shaded 95% confidence bands, with the log-rank p-value in the title for two-group comparisons.

parts.title: Patient profile form
parts.summary: Collects one patient's clinical values, biomarker statuses and treatments through sliders, a selectbox, radios and checkboxes.

parts.title: Recalibrated risk card and gauge
parts.summary: Fills a feature row from training defaults plus the form, runs the model and its Platt calibrator, and shows the probability as a card and a gauge marked with the cohort base rate, plus an interpretation note and a performance warning.

parts.title: Top-5 feature importances
parts.summary: Shows the five most important features of the global model as a horizontal bar chart.

parts.title: 5-year mortality prediction page
parts.summary: Puts the profile inputs on the left and the live prediction result on the right.
